subject: Cadenza-10B onboarding + temporary version pin request
messages:
From: Amy Zimmerman <amy.z@quantumretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-22T09:15:00Z
Subject: Request: onboard Cadenza-10B (partner) + version pin

Hi Evelyn / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Quantum Retail has completed internal validation of a partner model (Cadenza-10B) that we'd like Redwood to host for us as part of our merchandising personalization pipeline. Before we proceed, the compliance team requires a short period where the production route is pinned to a single verified artifact while we complete an audit — ideally ~2-3 weeks.

High-level asks: 
- Can Redwood ingest and serve Cadenza-10B (float16 or quantized 4-bit variants)?
- Can we request a temporary version pin for a stable build during our audit window?
- Any known incompatibilities with your current runtime (attention optimizations / KV cache behavior)?

I've attached the partner's compatibility notes and our evaluation logs. 

Attachments: compatibility-matrix-cadenza-10b.xlsx, onboard-checklist-QR-v1.pdf

Proposed timeline: pin starts Mon Feb 28, revert or revise by Mar 21.

Appreciate a quick confirmation and any gaps you see.

—Amy
Amy Zimmerman
Director, ML Engineering
Quantum Retail
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Zimmerman <amy.z@quantumretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-22T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: onboard Cadenza-10B (partner) + version pin

Amy — thanks for the materials and timeline. Looping in product and infra to assess compatibility and pin feasibility.

Laura: can you confirm whether temporary pins for partner artifacts are acceptable from a product / roadmap perspective and whether this should run through the standard gated onboarding flow or an exception?

Dev / Vivek: please review the attached matrix and CFP (audit ask) and advise on:
- runtime compatibility (kernel/attn/quantization paths)
- whether a temporary immutable pin is feasible in our serving infra and what constraints (autoscale, failover) we should enforce
- tests / smoke checks we need before flipping any production route

I think a 2–3 week pin is reasonable if we put clear rollback and canary rules in place. If we need an exception, call it out so we can route to leadership.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amy Zimmerman <amy.z@quantumretail.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-22T14:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: onboard Cadenza-10B (partner) + version pin

Quick technical read — skimmed the partner notes. Early observations:

1) Model shape & ops: Cadenza-10B appears standard transformer; no custom CUDA ops called out. Good chance the native FP16 path will work.

2) Quantized 4-bit: Need the partner's exact quantization format (GPTQ vs newer block-quant). Our runtime supports multiple q4 kernels but not all off-the-shelf conversions are compatible. If they provide a GGUF containing an established q4 layout we can likely serve it with existing kernels.

3) KV cache behavior: the model claims standard cached kv layout; still want to run a 1k-context smoke with capped batch sizes to verify memory pressure. If the model uses atypical rotary embeddings or custom position encodings, that's a red flag.

4) Pin mechanics: we have a mechanism for immutable deployment pins per route. Operational constraints:
   - Pinned variant cannot autoscale beyond the reserved cap unless we temporarily bump quotas.
   - Canary traffic must be routed to a separate route (un-pinned) and then promoted; automatic fallbacks are possible but need explicit fallback images.

Requesting from Quantum / partner: 
- sample GGUF or HF checkpoint (if license permits) of the exact build you want pinned
- the quantization script / metadata if using q4
- a minimal eval set (we can run smoke ~24hrs)

I'll run a compatibility job once we have the artifact. If everything passes we can provision a pinned route and document the rollback.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amy Zimmerman <amy.z@quantumretail.com>
Date: 2027-02-23T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: onboard Cadenza-10B (partner) + version pin

Thanks — product is aligned with a short pinned window as long as we attach explicit SLOs and rollback criteria. Proposed process: 

1) Day 0 (Feb 28): ingest artifact into staging, run the infra compatibility job (Dev) + QA eval (product).
2) Day 1–2: internal canary at 5% traffic for 24–48h; monitor latency, error rate, and token cost delta.
3) Day 3: escalate to pinned-proc: promote to production route pinned to artifact A (pin duration 21 days). Pin will be an immutable label; changes require an explicit unpin+promote flow.
4) During pinned window: weekly quality checks and an automatic revert trigger if latency increases >25% or error rate >1% above baseline.

I will create the onboarding ticket and the canary playbook. If we need a formal leadership exception (longer than 21 days, or unusual infra changes) we'll surface it.

Amy — can you get us the GGUF / checkpoint and the small eval set (qa-evalset-cadenza-v2.jsonl) by EOD Feb 25? That will let us hit the Feb 28 staging target.

—Laura
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amy Zimmerman <amy.z@quantumretail.com>
Date: 2027-02-24T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: onboard Cadenza-10B (partner) + version pin

All — I approve a temporary 21-day pin under the following conditions: 

- Partner artifact must be immutable and hosted in a verified artifact store (we need checksums).
- We provision a dedicated capacity slab for the pinned route (to avoid noisy-neighbor regressions) — Dev, please size the slab; I suggest reserving 2x expected qps for the first week.
- RBAC: only product + partner ops can request unpin. Any unpin request must pass through a change window and be recorded in the audit log.
- Attach the canary playbook and link to the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2bC-cadenza-onboard

I've uploaded a quick compatibility matrix with our observations and a checklist (compatibility-matrix-cadenza-10b.xlsx). Once Dev confirms smoke results, we can greenlight Feb 28 staging.

Vivek
VP, Platform & Operations
